description: Fresh random sample from entire course - independent verification round

worst_phrases.english: When she saw me feeling nervous, he wasn't patient.
worst_phrases.portuguese: Quando ela me viu sentindo nervoso, ele não era paciente.
issues: Confusing pronoun switch (she to he) appears to be an error
Portuguese 'me viu sentindo nervoso' is grammatically awkward - should be 'me viu nervoso' or use reflexive construction
Sentence meaning is unclear due to pronoun inconsistency

worst_phrases.english: she told me she had a very good idea about how to do that differently
worst_phrases.portuguese: ela me disse que tomou uma ideia muito boa sobre como fazer isso de forma diferente
issues: Portuguese uses incorrect verb 'tomou' (took) instead of 'teve' (had) for 'had an idea'
Correct Portuguese: 'ela me disse que teve uma ideia muito boa...'
This is a significant translation error that would confuse learners

worst_phrases.english: I like feeling very well and going to speak English.
worst_phrases.portuguese: Eu gosto de sentir muito bem e ir falar inglês.
issues: English 'feeling very well' is unidiomatic - should be 'feeling well' or 'feeling good'
Portuguese missing reflexive 'me' - should be 'sentir-me muito bem'

systematic_issues: Occasional redundancy in English phrasing (e.g., 'yet' and 'now' together, 'at work in the office')
Some awkward temporal constructions in English
Missing reflexive pronouns in Portuguese in a few cases
One significant verb translation error ('tomou' vs 'teve' for 'had an idea')
